llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its marketing-analysis purpose but contains multiple inconsistencies and risky behaviors (undocumented network access, cross-skill/local-path coupling, filesystem writes outside the skill, and shell/exec usage) that the user should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (抖音爆款分析, 标题/脚本生成) align with the code and manifest that call TikHub and DeepSeek APIs and produce local memory files; requesting TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY is appropriate. However the registry metadata summary at the top reported no required env vars while manifest.yaml and SKILL.md do require those keys — an inconsistency between the registry entry and the shipped manifest/instructions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime code does expected things (call DeepSeek, fetch TikTok/Douyin results, save analysis to scripts/memory). Concerns: (1) chromeSearch opens douyin.com via a spawned Chrome process — network access to douyin.com is not listed in the skill allowlist/documentation; (2) the Python integration (cmd_vid_integration.py) hardcodes a path into the user's home (~/.openclaw-agent2/...) and will attempt to invoke another skill's script if present — this is cross-skill coupling and reads external paths not mentioned in SKILL.md; (3) the code may start/kill Xvfb and use pkill, execSync/exec with user-supplied keywords — shell/command injection risk if inputs are not safely handled; (4) the skill writes analysis and workflow files and may write outside the skill folder (see cmd_vid_integration out_dir calculated as two levels up + agent_data).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only) — that's lower risk for supply-chain/remote download. Still, the code expects many local binaries (chrome/chromium, ffmpeg, whisper) and uses exec/execSync to run them; those runtime dependencies increase attack surface and may require elevated privileges or allow lateral actions (process killing, starting Xvfb).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested credentials (TIKHUB_TOKEN, DEEPSEEK_KEY) are appropriate for pulling Douyin/TikHub data and calling DeepSeek for AI generation. That said: (a) the top-level registry metadata incorrectly listed no required env vars while manifest and SKILL.md do require them; (b) the code also reads standard DISPLAY / DESKTOP_SESSION env vars to decide desktop vs headless behavior — those are normal but worth noting because they affect whether the skill will launch a visible browser on a user's desktop.

dimensions.detail: always:false and agentPolicy.modifiesOtherSkillsOrGlobalAgent:false (good). But the skill performs actions that persist data (writes scripts/memory/*.json) and may create an agent_data directory outside the skill tree. More concerning: it attempts to invoke a script from a hard-coded path in the user's home (~/.openclaw-agent2/.../chanjing-one-click-video-creation/scripts/run_render.py) which reaches into other skills' workspace — this cross-skill/local-path coupling can interact with files or code outside the skill's declared scope.

llm.guidance:
This skill mostly does what its description says, but there are several red flags you should consider before installing or running it: 

- Confirm required env vars: the manifest and SKILL.md require TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY — provide only tokens with minimal privileges and never paste secrets into files tracked by version control. Prefer environment variables as recommended. 

- Network allowances: the code fetches Douyin pages by launching Chrome against https://www.douyin.com, but the manifest's allowlist only documents api.tikhub.io and api.deepseek.com. Expect the skill to access additional hosts when using browser mode. If you must run it, isolate it (container/VM) or restrict network access. 

- Local binaries & process control: the skill runs external programs (chrome, ffmpeg, whisper), may start Xvfb and uses pkill — these can affect your system processes. Don't run it on a machine where stopping/starting processes is risky. 

- Cross-skill / path surprises: the Python integration tries to call a hard-coded script under ~/.openclaw-agent2/... which means it will look outside the skill directory and try to run other local tooling if present. Inspect or remove that integration if you don't want cross-skill interactions. 

- Filesystem writes: the skill writes memory files and may create directories outside the skill folder (agent_data). Review where it writes and prefer running in an isolated workspace. 

- Code-review advice: if you plan to use it, review marketing_hub.js and cmd_vid_integration.py yourself (or run under code review) to ensure inputs are sanitized and to remove any calls that reach into unexpected paths. Run the skill in a disposable container or VM, supply only minimal API credentials, and avoid giving it access to sensitive hosts or system-level permissions.
